title: Why are the lines through the hexagon's centre straight?
description: In a regular hexagon made of six equilateral triangles round the centre O, the lines AOD, BOE and COF are straight. Three angles of sixty degrees add to a straight angle of one hundred and eighty degrees. Keeko's doubt, that the lines look straight in the drawing, is tested and struck out.
teaching_notes: One idea: three angles of sixty degrees side by side make a straight angle. Watch for students who say the lines are straight because they look straight.

source: In Fig. 6.12 can you explain why AOD, BOE and COF are straight lines?
video_script.why: The child knows the angles of an equilateral triangle but has not yet used them to show that three points lie on one straight line.
video_script.substitution: Angles side by side that add up to a straight angle have outer arms pointing in opposite directions, so they form a straight line.
video_script.anchor: In a regular hexagon ABCDEF made of six equilateral triangles round the centre O: explain why AOD, BOE and COF are straight lines.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says AOD must be a straight line because it looks straight. A drawing can bend a tiny bit and still look straight, so a reason from the angles is needed.
video_script.payoff_line: Each is one hundred and eighty degrees, a straight angle

final_answer.value: Each of ∠AOD, ∠BOE and ∠COF is three 60° angles, which is 180°, a straight angle
final_answer.spoken: each of angle eigh O D, B O E and C O F is three sixty degree angles, which is one hundred and eighty degrees, a straight angle

never_show: the straight line AD drawn before step three
maths_rules: Angles AOB, BOC and COD are angles of equilateral triangles, so each is 60 degrees.
Angle AOD = angle AOB + angle BOC + angle COD = 60 + 60 + 60 = 180 degrees; added in steps: 60 + 60 = 120, 120 + 60 = 180.
An angle of 180 degrees is a straight angle, so OA and OD point in opposite directions and AOD is a straight line.
In the same way angle BOE = 180 degrees and angle COF = 180 degrees, so BOE and COF are straight lines too.
video_script.design: One idea: three angles of sixty degrees make a straight angle. Keeko's doubt is that the lines look straight. The straight line is drawn only after the angle sum is shown.
